tools.name: wf_readme
tools.description: Read this first before using any other WeaveFox MCP tools. Provides a guide on how to use WeaveFox open capabilities.

tools.name: wf_get_me
tools.description: Get the current authenticated user profile

tools.name: wf_create_app
tools.description: Create a new app. Currently only supports external (WeaveFox Pages) app type that hosts web app artifacts.

tools.name: wf_list_apps
tools.description: List apps of the current authenticated user with pagination

tools.name: wf_update_app
tools.description: Update an app name, description, tags, cover image, visibility status, custom domain URL, etc.

tools.name: wf_send_message
tools.description: Send a message to the app agent to iterate on app features. The agent runs asynchronously; use get_message to poll status.

tools.name: wf_get_message
tools.description: Get the status and content of the app agent message

tools.name: wf_list_messages
tools.description: List messages of an app with pagination, sorted by creation time in descending order.

tools.name: wf_stop_message
tools.description: Stop the running agent stream of an app.

tools.name: wf_get_upload_token
tools.description: Get a short-lived upload token for uploading an artifact zip file. Use the returned token as Bearer token in the Authorization header when calling the upload URL.

tools.name: wf_pages_create_version
tools.description: Create a new version of a WeaveFox Pages app from a local prebuilt artifact (zip). artifactZipUrl must be the URL returned by the artifact upload API.

tools.name: wf_list_versions
tools.description: List versions of an app with pagination, sorted by creation time descending.

tools.name: wf_deploy_version
tools.description: Deploy a specific version of a WeaveFox Pages app to make it live.

tools.name: wf_get_docs
tools.description: Get WeaveFox documentation links for LLM-friendly reading, including a concise summary and a full-text version.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "wf_readme" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Read this first before using any other WeaveFox MCP tools. Provides a guide on how to use WeaveFox open capabilities.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "wf_get_upload_token" references sensitive artifacts (authorization, bearer). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

evidence.snippet: Get a short-lived upload token for uploading an artifact zip file. Use the returned token as Bearer token in the Authorization header when calling the upload UR…

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: wf_get_message, wf_list_messages, wf_get_upload_token · Private data: wf_get_upload_token · Public sink: wf_send_message, wf_get_upload_token, wf_pages_create_version.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: wf_get_message, wf_list_messages, wf_get_upload_token · Private data: wf_get_upload_token · Public sink: wf_send_message, wf_get_upload_token, wf_pages_create_version

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
